estimates.narrative: Starting from a cautious baseline in the reference class, multiple updates from OPCW findings and credible intelligence push the probability toward 58%. Attribution uncertainty and deterrence dampen the rise, but escalation dynamics keep the risk non-zero and the calibrated range acknowledges remaining uncertainty.
summary: Posterior probability that a state actor will use chemical weapons in Ukraine before May 1, 2026 is 58% after updating from baseline forecasts.
OPCW-confirmed presence of riot-control agents (CS) on battlefield samples and credible intelligence of Russia increasing chemical-weapon activity push the risk upward.
Attribution uncertainty and ongoing investigations temper the update, while international norms and monitoring exert downward pressure.
Escalation dynamics in ongoing fighting keep the risk non-negligible, resulting in a calibrated range around the point estimate.

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence reporting Russia increasing use of banned chemical agents (chloropicrin/CS)

causal-factors.name: International norms and monitoring under the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC)
causal-factors.rationale: Ongoing surveillance and the prohibition on riot-control agents as weapons reduce incentives to escalate to full chemical-weapon use.

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed presence of riot-control agents (e.g., CS) in Ukraine-related samples
causal-factors.rationale: Documented CS detections on or near the battlefield suggest chemical agents are being used in the conflict, raising the base risk.

causal-factors.name: Intelligence reports of increased chemical weapons use by Russia
causal-factors.rationale: Credible intelligence accounts of higher suspected usage elevate the forecasted probability.

causal-factors.name: International deterrence and legal norms under the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) and OPCW
causal-factors.rationale: Global norms and verification efforts deter use and may counter escalation, suppressing the probability despite signals of activity.

causal-factors.name: Attribution uncertainty and misattribution risk
causal-factors.rationale: Ambiguity about who conducted alleged incidents reduces confidence in the forecast and mitigates a clear upward or downward move from the anchor.

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed presence of riot-control agents (CS) on Ukrainian front lines
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW analyses confirmed CS in multiple Ukraine incidents (Nov 2024, Feb 2025), indicating chemical agent deployment in the conflict and raising the likelihood of state-actor involvement.

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence assessments of Russia increasing chemical weapons use (chloropicrin and CS)
causal-factors.rationale: Dutch and German intelligence reports claim Russia has stepped up use of banned agents, signaling escalation that could translate into state-actor deployments.

causal-factors.name: Attribution uncertainty and ongoing OPCW investigations
causal-factors.rationale: While CS findings are documented, assigning responsibility to a specific state remains unresolved, yielding neither clear validation nor refutation of state use.

causal-factors.name: International sanctions and normative pressure targeting chemical weapons usage
causal-factors.rationale: EU/partners’ sanctions and continued OPCW scrutiny increase costs for potential future use, exerting downward pressure on the probability.

causal-factors.name: Escalation dynamics and battlefield pressure (drone-enabled tactics, offensive operations)
causal-factors.rationale: Ongoing combat escalation and methods that lower the cost of exposing troops to danger (e.g., drones delivering agents) elevate the incentive to employ chemical weapons.

synthesis: The baseline ensemble sits near 0.48, but attribution uncertainty and deterrence pressures warrant a modest downward adjustment. CS detections keep the risk non-zero, yielding a calibrated probability around 0.46 with a plausible 0.38–0.54 range.
